report.summary: Reviewed cache.py chunk 1: sqlite-based per-file analysis cache with content-addressed keys, JSON serialization, and eviction logic.
risks: cache_root() | low | Uses environment variables to determine cache directory; fallback to home dir may be unexpected on Windows if LOCALAPPDATA not set. | Test on Windows with missing LOCALAPPDATA and XDG_CACHE_HOME to confirm fallback.
_evict_old_caches | low | Exception handling silently ignores all errors; could mask permission or filesystem issues. | Review if silent failure is acceptable; consider logging.
_parser_version | low | Reads parse.py from disk; if file is missing or unreadable, returns empty string, which may cause cache collisions. | Confirm that empty string fallback is safe.
enabled() | low | Checks environment variable DAEDALUS_NO_CACHE; only recognizes '1', 'true', 'TRUE'; case-sensitive. | Document acceptable values.
_MAX_CACHE_FILES | low | Hardcoded limit of 20 cache databases; may be too small for many repos. | Consider making configurable.

claims.text: The index cache in ``index.py`` is in-memory, so it dies with the process: every server restart re-pays the full scan.
claims.why: Refers to index.py, not present in this chunk.

claims.text: INVALIDATION: the key is a hash of the file's CONTENT (plus its path, language and ``ANALYSIS_VERSION``) -- deliberately NOT size+mtime.
claims.why: file_key() includes text, rel, spec_name, and ANALYSIS_VERSION; no size/mtime used.

claims.text: We read every file's bytes anyway, so hashing is nearly free, and unlike mtime it cannot go stale: touch-without-edit is a hit, edit-preserving-mtime is a miss.
claims.why: Claim about reading every file's bytes is not verifiable in this chunk.

claims.text: A stale cache silently reporting wrong code health would be worse than a slow scan, so the key is chosen so staleness is not representable.
claims.why: file_key() uses content hash, ensuring any change in content produces a different key.

claims.text: Failure policy: this is an optimization, never a correctness dependency. Any sqlite problem degrades to "no cache" and the build proceeds normally.
claims.why: Constructor catches all exceptions and sets self.conn = None; get_many returns empty dict when conn is None.

claims.text: 2: rows gained ``type_facts``. Bumped rather than left to the KeyError path in ``_decode``, so a row from the previous generation is DELETEd on open instead of merely failing to decode -- the two failures look the same from the outside but only one of them is stated.
claims.why: __init__ executes DELETE FROM files WHERE schema IS NOT ? using _SCHEMA, deleting rows with different schema.

claims.text: ``DAEDALUS_CACHE_DIR`` overrides it (tests point this at a temp dir so they never touch the real cache).
claims.why: Function checks DAEDALUS_CACHE_DIR first and returns that path if set.

claims.text: Digest of the extractor's own source, folded into every key.
claims.why: _parser_version() returns SHA256 of parse.py; file_key() includes _parser_version() output.

claims.text: ``ANALYSIS_VERSION`` is hand-maintained, so it only invalidates the cache if someone remembers to bump it. Changing how a unit is NAMED without bumping produces the worst available outcome: ``slice`` re-parses off disk and sees the new names while the index is served from cache with the old ones, so the resolver silently matches nothing and slices quietly degrade -- a silent failure introduced BY a fix. Hashing parse.py makes that unrepresentable. Unreadable source degrades to the manual constant alone (never break the build for an optimization).
claims.why: _parser_version() catches Exception and returns empty string; file_key() still includes ANALYSIS_VERSION.

claims.text: Content-addressed key. ``rel`` is included because analysis embeds the module path (CodeUnit.module), so the same bytes at two paths are two different results.
claims.why: file_key() includes rel and spec_name in the hash.

claims.text: Tokenizer identity. FileAnalysis.n_tokens rides this cache, and its value is whatever tokens.count_tokens' runtime encoder produced -- tiktoken cl100k_base when the optional dep is installed, else the chars/4 fallback. tiktoken is optional and installing/removing it changes no source byte, so without this segment every file is a cache HIT across that change: the cached n_tokens (old tokenizer) sums into total_tokens (the distill denominator) while the slice numerator is recounted under the NEW tokenizer -- a silent mixed-tokenizer ratio that slice.py still stamps whole_repo_tokens_exact=True. Keying on tokenizer identity turns that into a miss (recompute under the current tokenizer) instead.
claims.why: Refers to tokens.tokenizer_name() and tokens.count_tokens, not present in this chunk. tokenizer_name() is called but its implementation is elsewhere.

claims.text: JSON, not pickle: the cache file is on disk and pickle would make a tampered cache an arbitrary-code-execution vector.

Encoded as nested plain LISTS, positionally, in declaration-field order -- exactly the style ``units`` uses for ``CodeUnit``. Written out by hand rather than via ``dataclasses.astuple``/``asdict`` for two reasons: a reflective codec would silently start round-tripping a NEW field the moment one is added to ``parse.py`` (so the cache would carry a field this generation of the decoder does not know how to place), and it would hide the one thing that actually needs care below -- JSON has no tuple, so every ``tuple[str, ...]`` field must be RE-TUPLED on the way in. A list where extraction produced a tuple changes ``repr`` and dataclass equality, which is enough to break the byte-identity assertions the type layer is held to (a cache HIT would not equal a cache MISS).
claims.why: Encoding functions convert tuples to lists; decoding functions convert lists back to tuples (e.g., _dec_type uses tuple(r[6]), tuple(r[7])).

claims.text: Every field is read by subscript, never .get(<default>): a row written by an older encoder is missing keys, and a default would let it decode into a plausible-looking analysis carrying a wrong measurement (n_tokens=0 reads as "this file contributes nothing to the repo's token total"). KeyError here is caught by get_many and becomes a cache MISS -- recompute, not quietly-wrong. ANALYSIS_VERSION already separates the generations; this is the second lock on the same door.
claims.why: Claim about get_many catching KeyError is not verifiable in this chunk; get_many is incomplete and its error handling is not shown.

claims.text: JSON gives lists where extraction gave tuples; every consumer just iterates/unpacks, so this is shape-compatible.
claims.why: In _decode, py_imports and raw_imports are converted to tuples via list comprehension.

claims.text: Subscript, like every field above: a row from before the type layer has no such key, and a ``.get(PyTypeFacts())`` default would decode it into a plausible analysis claiming the file has NO types -- which is indistinguishable from a file that genuinely has none.
claims.why: _decode uses doc["type_facts"] subscript access; no default provided.

claims.text: Keep only the most recently used cache DBs.
claims.why: Function sorts by st_mtime and deletes the oldest beyond _MAX_CACHE_FILES.

claims.text: Each DB is named by a hash of the repo root, so a root that disappears leaves an orphan nothing will ever reopen -- and the test suite indexes throwaway temp repos, which would otherwise drop a new orphan in the user's profile on every run. The root is unrecoverable from the hash, so bound the directory by recency instead.
claims.why: Constructor computes tag from root hash; _evict_old_caches limits total DB files to _MAX_CACHE_FILES.

claims.text: Parent-process only. Workers never touch sqlite -- they return plain data and the parent commits it in one transaction, which keeps the concurrency story trivial (no cross-process DB locking).
claims.why: No evidence of workers or multiprocessing in this chunk.

observations.what: FileCache.__init__ creates table with schema INTEGER and payload BLOB; deletes rows with schema != _SCHEMA.
get_many is incomplete; only returns empty dict for edge cases.
cache_root() falls back to home directory if no env vars set; may create .cache/daedalus/structcore under home.
_evict_old_caches uses st_mtime; may not reflect last use if files are touched.
_parser_version reads parse.py from disk each call; cached via lru_cache.
